Subject: Spike in 5xx/timeouts from q3a-quant variant (prod)

Hi Mina / Ben,

We started seeing a sudden spike in 5xx and timeouts hitting the q3a-quant model in our US prod region around 08:45 PDT. Error rate jumped from ~0.4% to ~6% for a 20-minute window; we attached a short log snippet. The errors manifest as 504s and occasional 502s in our client telemetry.

Can you confirm whether there was a rollout or infra change on your side? This is impacting a handful of customer-facing flows (search fallback) — we have circuit-breakers but want to understand cause and ETA for mitigation.

Attachments: bh_error_rates-0914.png (screenshot), request-log-snippet.txt

Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/timeouts from q3a-quant variant (prod)

Following up with an engineering note. Quick summary: we observed elevated queue latency and kernel OOM/retry paths for the q3a-quant fast-path kernel on the A100 pool servicing Blue Horizon requests.

Immediate actions taken (09:25–09:33 PDT):
- Scaled up the pool by adding two nodes to absorb backlog (manual bump).
- Performed controlled failover: moved Blue Horizon routed requests to the q3a-fp (floating non-quant) model group for the affected subnet.
- Rolled back the recent kernel flag (kernel-simd-6) that was enabled on 09:10 for q3a-quant and disabled continuous batching at the pool-level for 15 minutes to reduce head-of-line.

Result: error rate fell back to baseline within ~8 minutes after failover. Attaching a perf snapshot showing queue depth and error rate alignment.

Next steps:
- We'll run a targeted repro on staging with kernel-simd-6 + quantized weights to reproduce and capture debug traces.
- If repro succeeds, we'll prepare a patch or revert recommendation for the kernel optimizer.

Attachments: perf-snapshot.png

—
Dylan Brooks
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.ai

Subject: Q3a-quant incident postmortem and next steps (Blue Horizon)

Hi Lynn — thanks again for the quick signal and for validating the recovery on your side. Below is a concise postmortem and the follow-up plan. High-level summary first, then technical detail and actions.

High-level summary:
- Incident: transient increase in 5xx and timeouts for the q3a-quant model (US-prod) due to a combination of kernel-simd-6 optimizer interactions with quantized weights that caused elevated queueing and retry paths on specific A100 kernels.
- Impact: ~20 minutes of elevated error rate (~6%), affecting request latency and causing fallback behavior for some Blue Horizon customers. No data exfiltration or integrity issues.
- Recovery: manual failover to q3a-fp and rollback of kernel flag reduced errors to baseline within ~8 minutes.

Root cause details (short):
- kernel-simd-6 enabled a new SIMD path intended to accelerate the quantized GEMM routine. Under certain micro-batching patterns (high prefix variance for Blue Horizon traffic) the SIMD path triggered an edge case where the kernel attempted an optimistic fused path that hit a rare memory reclamation path, causing transient kernel-level retries and queue buildup. These retries surfaced as 502/504 at the RPC boundary.

Evidence collected:
- Request traces and debug artifacts from the affected pool (attached in the shared postmortem).
- Repro on staging with instrumented A100 driver showed queue starvation when batching patterns matched the production prefix distribution.

Corrective actions (short-term):
- We will keep q3a-quant disabled for the Blue Horizon dedicated pool until the patch is validated.
- Revert kernel-simd-6 globally for q3a-quant until a safe optimizer patch lands (expected within 72 hours of this message).
- Improve automated canary checks to cover micro-batching distributions for high-variance customers.

Follow-up (long-term):
- Engineering will deliver a patch to the optimizer to remove the unsafe fused path and add defensive guards. Tentative ETA: 3 business days (work in progress).
- We'll run a canary plan with synthetic traffic that matches Blue Horizon's prefix pattern and monitor for regressions before re-enabling quant.
- We'll share a postmortem PDF and a drive link within 24 hours.

Action items assigned:
- Dylan: deliver the optimizer patch and staging repro (ETA 72 hours).
- Marissa: coordinate communications and an optional credit for impacted API units (discuss offline).
- Mina: schedule a follow-up sync for Tuesday to review canary results.

Attachment: q3a-postmortem-20260916.pdf (detailed traces + timeline)
Shared postmortem: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/q3a-postmortem-20260916

If you want a hand-off call with the eng team today, we can do a 30-min slot at 16:30 PDT. Otherwise we'll proceed with the plan above and update you as items close.
